mainTopic: Gifts to the poor and to the כהן: when the owner must deliver them, and the exact borders of the foreleg, thigh and jaw
overview: The amud opens by finishing a list of four doubtful cases where a גר is exempt, because each one is only about money owed to a כהן. רבין then gives his own version of ריש לקיש's contradiction about standing grain. Next, רב ששת rules that when no poor people come, the owner may keep the לקט, since it is for the poor and not for birds and bats. The גמרא challenges this from תרומה and מתנות כהונה, which the owner must make sure reach a כהן. It concludes that those gifts are different because the Torah uses the word 'giving' about them. The extra word תעזב is then explained as teaching about a vineyard made הפקר and harvested. A story about רבי אמי taking a sack of coins gets two answers: he took it for the poor, or an important person is different. Finally a new משנה defines the foreleg, thigh and jaw. The גמרא explains why the foreleg is the right one, what the jaw and maw include, and how the jaw's limit fits a ברייתא, and the chapter הזרוע והלחיים ends.

steps.title: The convert's four money doubts: he is exempt
steps.stepSummary: The list of a convert's doubtful cases ends: ראשית הגז, the מתנות, פדיון הבן and פדיון פטר חמור. In all of them he is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first shearing, the gifts, redeeming the firstborn son, and redeeming the firstborn donkey: in these he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a list of four cases where it is unclear whether a גר's obligation started before or after he converted. In all four, the ruling is that he is exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All four obligations are about giving money or property to a כהן. When we are in doubt about a money matter, the one who wants to take the money must prove his claim. So the כהן cannot force the גר to pay, and the גר is פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: The first portion of shorn wool, given to a כהן
The gifts of foreleg, jaw and maw from a slaughtered animal, given to a כהן
Redeeming a firstborn son from a כהן with five סלעים
Redeeming a firstborn donkey with a sheep or goat
Exempt; not obligated

steps.whatToRemember: A גר in doubt about these four gifts to a כהן is פטור, because each one is only a question of money.

phrases.english: The first shearing and the gifts,
and the redemption of the firstborn son,
and the redemption of a firstborn donkey: to exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a list that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the four doubtful cases (ראשית הגז, מתנות, פדיון הבן, פדיון פטר חמור), a גר is exempt.

steps.title: רבין's version: standing grain against standing grain
steps.stepSummary: רבין reports that ריש לקיש's contradiction was between two sources that both talk about standing grain (קמה).
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came, he said: He raised a contradiction between standing grain and standing grain.
steps.whatsHappening: רבין arrived from ארץ ישראל and gave a different report of the earlier argument between ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן. In his version, ריש לקיש compared two sources that both deal with standing grain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier version, the two sources ריש לקיש compared were about different situations. רבין says both were about קמה, standing grain. In one, רבי מאיר exempts a גר's standing grain from gleanings when there is a doubt. In the other, grain that might be gleanings is treated as gleanings. That makes the contradiction sharper, and רבי יוחנן's answer stays the same.

keyTerms.meaning: Standing grain, not yet harvested
He raised a contradiction between two sources
When [a sage] came from ארץ ישראל to Babylonia

phrases.english: When Ravin came, he said:
He raised a contradiction between standing grain and standing grain.
phrases.notes: 'He' is ריש לקיש, from the earlier discussion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different report of the contradiction discussed before this section.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's view on a convert's doubtful gleanings
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One source has רבי מאיר exempting a convert's standing grain when there is a doubt. Another source, also about standing grain, treats doubtful gleanings as gleanings.

steps.title: No poor people around: the gleanings are not for birds
steps.stepSummary: לוי planted in כישר, where no poor people came to take לקט. רב ששת told him the gleanings are for the poor, not for ravens and bats, so he could keep them.
steps.simpleTranslation: לוי planted in כישר, and there were no poor people to take gleanings. He came before רב ששת, who said to him: 'You shall leave them for the poor and for the stranger', and not for ravens or bats.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story. לוי asked what to do with gleanings when no poor people were around, and רב ששת answered that he did not have to leave them to go to waste.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says to leave the gleanings for the poor and the stranger. רב ששת reads this as a statement of purpose: the מצוה exists so the poor can benefit. If no poor people will come, leaving the grain only feeds animals, so the owner may take it himself.

keyTerms.meaning: Gleanings: stalks that fall during harvest and must be left for the poor
Poor people
Ravens
Bats

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets up the question of whether a gift for the poor or for a כהן may be taken back by the owner when no one is there to receive it. The next step challenges this.

phrases.english: Levi sowed in Kishar,
and there were no poor people to take gleanings.

phrases.aramaic: אֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב שֵׁשֶׁת, אֲמַר לֵיהּ:
phrases.english: He came before Rav Sheshet, who said to him:
"You shall leave them for the poor and for the stranger,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:22

phrases.english: and not for ravens and not for bats.
phrases.notes: In other words, no one should leave the grain just for birds and bats to eat, so לוי may take it himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about gifts to the poor.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If no poor people are present to take לקט, the owner does not have to leave it to rot or be eaten by animals; he may take it.

steps.title: Challenge from תרומה: the owner must bring it to town
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the owner usually does not bring תרומה to the כהן. But if no כהן is there, he must hire a cow and bring it to town so the תרומה is not lost.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: One does not bring תרומה from the threshing floor to the city, or from the wilderness to a settled area. But if there is no כהן there, he hires a cow and brings it, because of the loss of תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב ששת's ruling with a ברייתא about תרומה. The answer to this challenge comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the כהן has to come to the field to collect his תרומה. If no כהן is there, the owner may not simply let it go to waste; he even has to pay to transport it to town. If that is the rule for תרומה, why should לוי be allowed to take the gleanings when no poor people are present? He should have to bring them to the poor.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce given to a כהן
Threshing floor
A settled, inhabited area
Loss or waste of תרומה

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא does not say the owner must always deliver תרומה. Usually he does not. Only when no כהן is present must he bring it, so that it is not lost.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
One does not bring teruma,
neither from the threshing floor to the city,
nor from the wilderness to a settled area,
but if there is no priest there,
he hires a cow and brings it,
because of the loss of teruma.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב ששת's ruling from Step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's ruling that לוי may take the gleanings when no poor people are present
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The owner must make an effort, even at a cost, so that תרומה is not lost when no כהן is present. By comparison, he should also have to bring the לקט to the poor rather than take it for himself.

steps.title: תרומה is different because it makes the crop טבל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the question from Step 4: תרומה makes the whole crop טבל, so it must be separated. לקט does not do that.
steps.simpleTranslation: תרומה is different, because until it is taken off, the crop is טבל and may not be eaten. So there is no way around separating it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction from Step 4 between לקט and תרומה. It says תרומה is in a special category because it makes the crop טבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If תרומה is not separated, the whole crop is forbidden as טבל. So the owner cannot skip it, and he must deal with it properly. לקט does not forbid the rest of the field, so when no poor people come, the owner may keep it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different
It makes the crop טבל, forbidden until the gifts are taken off
It is impossible / there is no way around it
Separates, sets aside the required portion

phrases.english: Terumah is different, since it makes the crop tevel,
phrases.notes: טבל is produce whose gifts have not been taken off yet. You may not eat it until they are.

phrases.english: and it is impossible for him not to separate it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (חילוק): תרומה makes the crop טבל and לקט does not.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: תרומה and לקט look alike, since both are gifts from the crop, so they should follow the same rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: תרומה must be dealt with because it makes the crop טבל. לקט does not, so the owner may keep it.

steps.title: Challenge from מתנות כהונה, which do not make the animal טבל
steps.stepSummary: מתנות כהונה do not make the animal טבל. Still, a ברייתא says the owner must protect the כהן's share and even pay him its value when no כהן is there.
steps.simpleTranslation: But look at the gifts of the כהן (the foreleg, jaw and stomach). They do not make the animal טבל. Yet a ברייתא teaches: where people scald calves in boiling water to eat them with the skin, the owner may not skin the foreleg before giving it. Where people skin the head, he may not skin the jaw. And if no כהן is there, the owner puts a price on the gifts, eats them, and owes the money, so the כהן does not lose out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of Step 5. It brings מתנות כהונה, which do not make anything טבל, yet the owner must still make sure the כהן gets his share.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 said the owner must take care of תרומה only because it causes טבל. מתנות do not cause טבל, yet the ברייתא still makes the owner protect the כהן's gifts, and even pay their value when no כהן is around. So 'טבל' cannot be the full reason, and the question of why לקט is different comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: The gifts a כהן gets from a slaughtered animal: foreleg, jaw and stomach
To scald in hot water to remove the hair, leaving the skin on the meat
Foreleg, one of the gifts
Jaw or cheek, one of the gifts
They set a money value on them
The loss to the כהן

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the two questions apart. The ברייתא here is about מתנות from an animal, not about תרומה. The point is that the owner must protect the gift even though it does not cause טבל.

phrases.english: But what about the gifts, which do not make the animal tevel?
And it was taught in a baraita:
In a place where they are used to scalding calves,
phrases.notes: In such a place people eat the skin along with the meat, so the skin is worth something to the כהן.

phrases.english: he may not skin the foreleg.
Where they are used to skinning the head,
he may not skin the jaw.
And if there is no kohen there,
they put a money value on them and eat them,
because of the kohen's loss.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that תרומה is different because it makes the crop טבל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Here is a counter-example: מתנות do not cause טבל, yet the owner must still protect the כהן's share. So the טבל reason does not explain why לקט may be kept.

steps.title: מתנות are different because the Torah writes 'giving'
steps.stepSummary: The Torah uses the word 'giving' for מתנות כהונה, so the owner must actually give them. No such word is written for לקט.
steps.simpleTranslation: מתנות כהונה are different, because the Torah writes the word 'giving' about them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge of Step 6. It says מתנות have their own reason: the פסוק says 'and he shall give to the כהן'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the Torah says 'give', the owner has an active duty to make sure the gifts reach a כהן. That is why he must pay their value if no כהן is there. לקט is only left in the field for the poor, with no command to give it, so when no poor people come, the owner may keep it.

keyTerms.meaning: Giving, an active handing over
It is written about it in the Torah
The priestly gifts

phrases.english: The gifts of the kehunah are different,
since 'giving' is written about them.
phrases.notes: דברים 18:3

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי מַתְּנוֹת כְּהוּנָּה, דִּנְתִינָה כְּתִיבָא בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A reason based on a פסוק: the Torah uses a word of giving.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The only reason to make sure a gift reaches its owner is טבל, so מתנות should be like לקט.
steps.terutzMaskana: Any gift the Torah describes with 'giving' must actively reach the person it belongs to.

steps.title: The 'giving' reason also explains תרומה
steps.stepSummary: Now that 'giving' explains מתנות, the גמרא says the same reason explains תרומה too, since the Torah also writes 'giving' about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you have reached this answer, תרומה also has 'giving' written about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up by using the new reason for תרומה as well. It replaces the earlier 'טבל' answer from Step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner must bring תרומה to a כהן because the Torah says 'you shall give him'. The reason is not that תרומה causes טבל. So one rule now covers both cases: gifts with 'giving' written about them must reach the person they belong to, and לקט, which has no such word, may be kept when no poor people come.

keyTerms.meaning: Now that you have arrived at this answer
Also

steps.whatToRemember: The difference is the Torah's word 'giving'. תרומה and מתנות כהונה must actively reach the כהן, even with effort or payment. לקט has no command to give, so when no poor people come, the owner keeps it.
steps.whyThisMatters: It gives one clear rule for priestly gifts: the duty comes from the command to give, not from whether the food is forbidden as טבל.

phrases.english: Now that you have come to this,
terumah also has 'giving' written about it.
phrases.notes: דברים 18:4

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the answer of Step 7 and uses it for תרומה, replacing the answer of Step 5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both תרומה and מתנות כהונה must reach the כהן because the Torah says 'give'. לקט, which has no such word, may be kept by the owner when no poor people come.

steps.title: Why does the Torah say 'you shall leave' twice?
steps.stepSummary: If לקט does not need to be actively given, the גמרא asks why the Torah repeats the word תַּעֲזֹב.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then why do I need the extra 'you shall leave'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא just said there is no word of 'giving' for לקט, so the owner does not have to bring it to the poor. Now it asks why the Torah writes 'you shall leave' a second time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah writes 'you shall leave them for the poor' in two places. If one time is enough to teach that the owner must leave לקט, the second time seems extra. That extra word might suggest the owner must protect לקט for the poor after all, which would go against Step 8.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You shall leave'. The Torah's word for leaving gifts in the field for the poor.
Extra, more than needed
Gleanings. Stalks that fall during harvest and belong to the poor.

phrases.english: But then, why do I need the extra "you shall leave"?
phrases.notes: 'You shall leave them for the poor' shows up twice, in ויקרא 19:10 and ויקרא 23:22, so the second one looks extra.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of Step 8 by pointing to an extra word in the פסוק
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the owner has no duty to actively hand לקט over to the poor
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An extra תַּעֲזֹב must teach something. It might teach that the owner must make sure the poor actually get the לקט.

steps.title: The extra word teaches about a vineyard that was made ownerless and then harvested
steps.stepSummary: The extra תַּעֲזֹב teaches that a man who makes his vineyard הפקר and harvests it the next morning still has to leave the gifts for the poor, though he is exempt from מעשרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed for what a ברייתא teaches: if someone makes his vineyard ownerless, then gets up early the next morning and harvests it, he must still leave פרט, עוללות, שכחה, and פאה for the poor. But he does not have to separate מעשרות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the extra 'you shall leave' is not about bringing gifts to the poor. It teaches a different case, found in a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually an ownerless field is free from the gifts to the poor. Here the owner gave up the vineyard and then took it back by harvesting it. The extra תַּעֲזֹב teaches that he must still leave the poor their gifts. He is still exempt from מעשרות, because the grapes came to him from הפקר.

keyTerms.meaning: One who declares his property ownerless (הֶפְקֵר), so that anyone may take it
Single grapes that fall during the harvest. They belong to the poor.
Small, poorly formed grape clusters. They belong to the poor.
Produce forgotten in the field. It belongs to the poor.
The corner of the field, left for the poor
Tithes taken from produce

steps.whatToRemember: The extra תַּעֲזֹב does not teach that the owner must bring לקט to the poor. It teaches that gifts to the poor apply even to a vineyard that was made הפקר and then harvested.

phrases.english: It is needed for what was taught: One who makes his vineyard ownerless,
and got up early the next morning and harvested it,
is obligated in fallen single grapes and in small clusters,
and in forgotten clusters and in the corner of the field,
and he is exempt from the tithes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 9 by giving the extra word a different job
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the extra word a different job (לגופיה / reassigning the extra source)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The extra תַּעֲזֹב means the owner must make sure the poor get the לקט
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra תַּעֲזֹב includes a vineyard made הפקר and then harvested in the gifts to the poor

steps.title: רבי אמי takes a sack of coins brought to the בית מדרש
steps.stepSummary: A sack of dinars sent to the בית מדרש arrived, and רבי אמי rushed to acquire it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A sack of dinars was once brought to the study hall. רבי אמי rushed and took possession of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story connected to taking gifts meant for others. It is setting up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The money was sent to support the people of the בית מדרש, like a gift for the poor. רבי אמי moved quickly and acquired it. This looks like taking the gift himself instead of waiting to be given it.

keyTerms.meaning: A sack of dinars (coins)
The study hall
Acquired, took legal ownership

phrases.english: There was a certain sack of dinars
that came to the study hall,
Rabbi Ami rushed ahead and acquired them.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא שַׂקָּא דְּדִינָרֵי דַּאֲתָא לְבֵי מִדְרְשָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the פסוקים to a real story about taking gifts
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אמי acquired the coins that were brought to the בית מדרש

steps.title: How could he take it, if gifts must be given?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי אמי could take the coins himself, since the Torah says 'and he shall give', meaning one should not take a gift on his own.
steps.simpleTranslation: How could he do this? The Torah writes 'and he shall give', which means the receiver should not take it by himself!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אמי's action. It uses the 'giving' idea from Step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 taught that the word 'giving' means the gift must be handed over by the owner. If so, the receiver may not just grab it. רבי אמי seems to have done exactly that.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And he shall give'. Shows that a gift must be handed over.
That he take it by himself, without being given it

phrases.english: But how could he do this?
But isn't it written: "And he shall give,"
phrases.notes: דברים 18:3. This פסוק is about gifts to a כהן. The גמרא uses the same idea for money for the poor.

phrases.english: and not that he should take it by himself!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the action described in the story of Step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אמי's taking of the coins
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Torah's word 'giving' means a gift may not be taken by the receiver on his own

steps.title: He took the coins for the poor
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי did not take the money for himself. He acquired it for the poor.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי also acquired them for the poor, not for himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אמי did nothing wrong. He took the coins on behalf of the poor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule against taking applies to someone who takes a gift for himself. Here רבי אמי acted for the poor, to look after the money for them. So he was not 'taking for himself' at all.

keyTerms.meaning: For the poor
Also, too

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אַמֵּי נָמֵי לַעֲנִיִּים זָכָה בָּהֶן.
phrases.english: Rabbi Ami, too, acquired them for the poor.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַמֵּי נָמֵי לַעֲנִיִּים זָכָה בָּהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: he acted for others, not for himself
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אמי took the coins for himself
steps.terutzMaskana: He acquired them on behalf of the poor, so the rule of 'giving' was not broken

steps.title: An important person is different
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: an important person may take for himself. A ברייתא teaches that the כהן גדול should be greater than his brothers, even in wealth.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you want, say that an important person is different. A ברייתא teaches about 'the כהן who is greater than his brothers': he should be greater than them in beauty, in wisdom, and in wealth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another answer: רבי אמי was an important person, and the rules are different for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here we can say רבי אמי really did take the money for himself, and it was allowed. The ברייתא shows that the Torah wants a great person to stand above others, even in wealth. So it is proper for an important person to receive extra.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you want, say'. Brings in a second, different answer.
An important, distinguished person
Is different
The High Priest
Beauty
Wealth

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers for רבי אמי: (1) he took the coins for the poor; (2) an important person is different and may take for himself.

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
an important person is different,
as it was taught: "And the priest who is greater than his brothers"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:10

phrases.english: means that he should be greater than his brothers
in beauty, in wisdom, and in wealth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the קשיא of Step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Exception for a special person (אדם חשוב שאני)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No one may take a gift for himself
steps.terutzMaskana: An important person may take for himself, based on the ברייתא about the כהן גדול being greater even in wealth

steps.title: His brother כהנים must make the כהן גדול wealthy
steps.stepSummary: אחרים learn from the same פסוק that if the כהן גדול has no money, the other כהנים must give him wealth from their own.
steps.simpleTranslation: Others say: How do we know that if the כהן גדול has no money, his brother כהנים must make him great? The פסוק says 'the priest who is greater than his brothers', meaning make him great from what belongs to his brothers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the ברייתא it began in step 14. It adds that the other כהנים must actually give the כהן גדול money if he has none.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 only said the כהן גדול should be the richest. This opinion goes further: his wealth should come from his brothers. So if the people of the בית מדרש are obligated to make רבי אמי wealthy, he may certainly take the gift for himself.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Others': a name for an unnamed תנא who gives a different opinion
They make him great (here: rich)
Make him great from what belongs to his brothers

steps.whatToRemember: An important person, like a כהן גדול or a leading חכם, may take a gift for himself, and others should even help make him wealthy.

phrases.english: Others say:
From where do we know that if he does not have money,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the כהן גדול from the ברייתא in the step before.

phrases.english: that his brothers, the priests, make him great?
The verse says: "And the priest who is greater than his brothers":
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:10

phrases.english: make him great from what belongs to his brothers.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲחֵרִים אוֹמְרִים מִנַּיִן שֶׁאִם אֵין לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted in step 14, adding a stronger version of its lesson.
steps.raayaObject: The second answer, that an important person like רבי אמי may take a gift for himself.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The opinion of אחרים in the ברייתא, reading 'הגדול מאחיו' as 'make him great from his brothers' property'.

steps.title: The משנה defines the foreleg and its matching thigh
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says the זרוע runs from the knee joint up to the top of the foreleg. It is the same זרוע given from a נזיר's ram, and the matching piece on the hind leg is the שוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which part is the זרוע? From the knee joint up to the top part of the foreleg. That is the זרוע of the נזיר. The matching part on the hind leg is the שוק.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It tells us exactly which part of the animal counts as the זרוע that goes to the כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah says to give the זרוע but does not say where it begins and ends. The משנה sets its edges and says it is the same piece meant for the נזיר. It also uses it to define the שוק on the back leg, which comes from a קרבן שלמים.

keyTerms.meaning: The foreleg, one of the gifts given to the כהן
The knee joint
The top, rounded part of the foreleg
The thigh of the hind leg, given to the כהן from a קרבן שלמים
A person who took a vow of נזירות; a cooked foreleg of his ram goes to the כהן

phrases.english: MISHNAH: What is the foreleg?
From the joint of the knee
until the rounded top of the foreleg,
and that is the one of the nazirite,
and its parallel in the hind leg is the thigh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. The topic moves from the story of רבי אמי to the exact borders of the gifts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The זרוע is from the knee joint to the top of the foreleg. It is the same as the נזיר's זרוע, and the שוק is the matching piece on the hind leg.

steps.title: רבי יהודה gives a different border for the thigh
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says the שוק runs from the knee joint up to the upper joint of the leg.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: The שוק is from the knee joint until the upper joint of the leg.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with the first opinion about where the שוק ends.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion made the שוק match the זרוע exactly, reaching all the way up to the rounded top of the leg bone. רבי יהודה stops the שוק at the סובך, the joint between the middle and upper sections of the hind leg. So in his view the שוק is shorter and does not reach as high.

keyTerms.meaning: The upper joint of the hind leg

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: The thigh is
from the joint of the knee
until the upper joint of the leg.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר שׁוֹק מִן הַפֶּרֶק שֶׁל אַרְכוּבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second opinion on the שוק defined in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, the שוק reaches from the knee joint to the upper joint of the leg.

steps.title: The משנה defines the jaw
steps.stepSummary: The לחי runs from the jaw joint down to the ring of the windpipe.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which part is the לחי? From the joint of the jaw until the ring of the windpipe.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now defines the second gift, the jaw.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the זרוע, the Torah names the לחי without giving its borders. The משנה gives them: from the jaw joint down to the top ring of the windpipe.

keyTerms.meaning: The jaw, one of the gifts given to the כהן
The ring of the windpipe

phrases.english: What is the jaw?
From the joint of the jaw
until the ring of the windpipe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה, moving from the זרוע to the לחי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The לחי is from the jaw joint until the ring of the windpipe.

steps.title: A ברייתא teaches that the foreleg is the right one
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the word 'הזרוע' that the gift is the right foreleg, not the left.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'The foreleg' means the right foreleg. Do you say it is the right one, or maybe it is the left? The פסוק says 'the foreleg'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא saying which foreleg goes to the כהן: the right one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא asks whether it could be the left foreleg. It answers from the word 'הזרוע', but it does not explain how that word shows it is the right one. The next step asks exactly that.

keyTerms.meaning: The right foreleg
The left foreleg
'The verse says': the source that answers the question

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
"The foreleg": this is the right foreleg.
phrases.notes: דברים 18:3

phrases.english: Do you say this is the right foreleg,
or is it only the left foreleg?
The verse says: "the foreleg."

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן הַזְּרוֹעַ זֶה זְרוֹעַ יָמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא adds a detail to the משנה's זרוע: which side of the animal it comes from.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The זרוע given to the כהן is the right foreleg, learned from the word 'הזרוע'.

steps.title: How does 'the foreleg' show it is the right one?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the word 'הזרוע' proves it means the right foreleg.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the proof from this word?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the ברייתא learned its rule. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just saying 'הזרוע' does not clearly point to the right side. The גמרא wants to know what in this word teaches 'right'.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the proof? How is this learned from the פסוק?

phrases.english: What is the derivation?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the ברייתא's proof in step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the word 'הזרוע' shows that the right foreleg is meant.

steps.title: 'The' means the most important one, as רבא taught
steps.stepSummary: Just as רבא learned that 'הירך' in the פסוק of גיד הנשה means the most important thigh, 'הזרוע' means the most important foreleg, the right one.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבא said: 'the thigh' means the most important thigh. Here too, 'the foreleg' means the most important foreleg.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers using a rule of רבא: the word 'the' points to the most important one, which is the right side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא learned from 'הירך' in the פסוק of גיד הנשה that 'the' points to the most important thigh. The גמרא uses the same rule for 'הזרוע': it means the most important foreleg. The right side is treated as the more important side, so the gift is the right foreleg.

keyTerms.meaning: The most important, the chosen one (the right side)
Thigh: from the פסוק about גיד הנשה
Here too, the same rule applies

steps.whatToRemember: The 'ה' in 'הזרוע' points to the most important foreleg, so the כהן gets the right foreleg.
steps.confusionAlert: The word 'right' never appears in the פסוק. It comes only from the word 'the', read as pointing to the most important one.

phrases.english: As Rava said:
"The thigh" means the most important thigh,
phrases.notes: בראשית 32:33, the פסוק about גיד הנשה.

phrases.english: here too:
"The foreleg" means the most important foreleg.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'the' means the most important one, as רבא taught about 'הירך'. So 'הזרוע' is the most important foreleg, the right one.

steps.title: What does the word 'and the jaw' come to add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what extra law is learned from the ה in 'והלחיים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the jaw': what does this come to teach?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is looking closely at the word 'והלחיים' in the פסוק and asks what extra thing it teaches. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have just said 'לחיים'. Instead it says 'הלחיים', with the extra ה, 'the jaw'. The גמרא assumes extra letters come to add something and asks what that is.

keyTerms.meaning: The jaw (the cheeks), one of the three gifts to the כהן
What does it come for? (What is it teaching?)

phrases.english: 'And the jaw': what does it come for?
phrases.notes: This is from the פסוק of the gifts, דברים 18:3. The extra ה, 'the', is what is being asked about.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Keeps reading the פסוק of the gifts word by word, now moving from the foreleg to the jaw.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What extra law the ה of 'והלחיים' teaches.

steps.title: The jaw includes the wool and beard hair
steps.stepSummary: The extra ה adds the wool on a sheep's head and the beard hair of goats to the gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to include the wool on the head of lambs and the hair in the beard of goats.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the extra ה teaches the wool and hair growing on the head are part of the jaw gift. So the owner may not shear them off first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without this, we might think only the meat of the jaw goes to the כהן. The ה tells us the whole jaw goes, including the wool or hair growing on it.

keyTerms.meaning: To include (to add something to the law)
Wool
The beard of goats

phrases.english: To include the wool that is on the head of lambs,
and the hair that is in the beard of goats.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ה adds the wool and beard hair on the head, so they go to the כהן along with the jaw.

steps.title: What does the word 'and the maw' come to add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what extra law is learned from the ה in 'והקבה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the maw': what does this come to teach?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same kind of question about the third gift, the קבה. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here too the פסוק says 'הקבה', 'the maw', with an extra ה. The גמרא wants to know what this extra letter adds.

keyTerms.meaning: The maw (the fourth stomach of a cow or sheep), one of the gifts

phrases.english: 'And the maw': what does it come for?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same question pattern as step 22, now for the maw.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What extra law the ה of 'והקבה' teaches.

steps.title: The maw includes its fat
steps.stepSummary: The extra ה adds the fat on top of the maw and the fat inside it to the gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to include the fat that is on the maw and the fat that is inside the maw.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the fat on the maw and inside it also belongs to the כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without this, one might think the כהן gets only the maw itself. The ה teaches that the fat attached to it is part of the gift too.

keyTerms.meaning: Fat (here, the fat attached to the maw)
On top of

phrases.english: To include the fat that is on top of the maw,
and the fat that is inside the maw.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ה adds the fat on and inside the maw to the כהן's gift.

steps.title: Proof from רבי יהושע that the fat belongs to the כהן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע said the כהנים were generous and let the owner keep the fat. That shows that without this generosity the fat would be theirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יהושע said: the כהנים acted generously with it and gave it to the owners. The reason is only that they acted generously; if they had not, it would be his, the כהן's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support that the maw's fat really belongs to the כהן. רבי יהושע said the כהנים chose to give it up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You can only be generous with something that is yours. Since the כהנים gave the fat away as a kindness, the fat must belong to them by law. So the rule from step 25 is confirmed.

keyTerms.meaning: A generous eye, being generous
The owners (here, the owner of the animal)
The reason is only because..., but otherwise (a way of drawing an inference)
His (it belongs to him)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the custom of leaving the fat with the owner is a favor from the כהנים, not the basic law.

phrases.english: As רבי יהושע said:
The כהנים acted generously with it
and gave it to the owners.
The reason is that they acted generously,
but if they had not acted so, it would be his.
phrases.notes: 'His' means the כהן's. By law the fat goes to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: כֹּהֲנִים נָהֲגוּ בּוֹ עַיִן יָפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up the answer of step 25 with a statement of a sage.
steps.raayaObject: That the fat of the maw belongs to the כהן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהושע's statement that the כהנים gave the fat to the owners out of generosity, which shows it was really theirs.

steps.title: The foreleg matches פינחס's hand
steps.stepSummary: The דורשי חמורות say the foreleg gift matches the hand of פינחס, who took a spear in his hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: The interpreters of hidden meanings used to say: the foreleg matches the hand, as the פסוק says: 'And he took a spear in his hand.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives a deeper idea about why the כהן gets these three gifts. The first gift, the foreleg, matches the hand of פינחס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פינחס, a כהן, stopped the plague by killing the sinners with a spear in his hand. The foreleg is like the animal's 'hand', so it is given to the כהנים as a reward for that hand.

keyTerms.meaning: Interpreters of hidden or symbolic meanings in the Torah
Matching, corresponding to
A spear

phrases.english: The interpreters of hidden meanings used to say:
The foreleg matches the hand,
and so it says:
'And he took a spear in his hand.'
phrases.notes: במדבר 25:7, about פינחס.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the legal details of the gifts to the deeper reason behind them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The foreleg gift matches the hand of פינחס that held the spear.

steps.title: The jaw matches prayer and the maw matches the stomach
steps.stepSummary: The jaw matches פינחס's prayer, and the maw matches the woman's stomach that he pierced.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the jaw matches prayer, as it says: 'And פינחס stood up and prayed.' The maw is as it sounds, as it says: 'and the woman through her stomach.'
steps.whatsHappening: The דורשי חמורות finish their idea: the jaw stands for the prayer of פינחס, and the maw stands for the stomach of the woman he killed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Prayer comes out of the mouth, so the jaw matches it. The word 'ויפלל' is read as 'prayed'. The maw needs no hint, since the פסוק uses the very same word, 'קבתה', her stomach.

keyTerms.meaning: Prayer
And he prayed (or: he carried out judgment)
As it sounds, its plain meaning

steps.whatToRemember: All three gifts, the foreleg, jaw, and maw, are a reward to the כהנים for what פינחס did: his hand, his prayer, and the woman's stomach.

phrases.english: And the jaw matches prayer,
and so it says:
'And פינחס stood up and prayed.'
phrases.notes: תהלים 106:30.

phrases.english: The maw is as it sounds,
and so it says:
'and the woman through her stomach.'
phrases.notes: במדבר 25:8. פינחס speared her through the stomach.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the idea of step 27 for the other two gifts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The jaw matches פינחס's prayer, and the maw matches the woman's stomach.

steps.title: Another source: the foreleg of sacrifices from 'תרומה'
steps.stepSummary: A תנא learns the right foreleg from the 'right thigh' of a שלמים. The word 'תרומה' adds the foreleg of a sacrifice.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a תנא brings it from here: 'The right thigh.' I only know about the right thigh. How do I know about the foreleg of sacrifices? The פסוק says 'תרומה'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows a different source for the rule that the gift is the right foreleg. A תנא starts from the right thigh of a שלמים and widens it, step by step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 learned 'right' from the word 'הזרוע'. This תנא instead starts from 'שוק הימין', which clearly says right. The word 'תרומה' then adds the foreleg of a sacrifice (the נזיר's ram), so it is also the right one.

keyTerms.meaning: The right thigh (the כהן's portion of a שלמים)
Holy animals, sacrifices
The פסוק teaches (says)
A gift set aside for the כהן

phrases.english: And a תנא brings it from here:
phrases.notes: 'It' is the rule that the gift is the right foreleg, from step 19.

phrases.aramaic: ״שׁוֹק הַיָּמִין״ – אֵין לִי אֶלָּא שׁוֹק הַיָּמִין,
phrases.english: 'The right thigh': I only know about the right thigh.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:32, about the שלמים.

phrases.english: How do I know about the foreleg of sacrifices?
The פסוק says 'תרומה' (a gift).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the rule of step 19 and gives a different source for it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The right foreleg of a sacrifice is learned from the right thigh of a שלמים through the word 'תרומה'.

steps.title: The foreleg of ordinary animals from 'תתנו'
steps.stepSummary: The word 'תתנו' widens the rule to the foreleg of ordinary, non-holy animals, so it too must be the right one.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do I know about the foreleg of ordinary animals? The פסוק says 'you shall give.'
steps.whatsHappening: The תנא takes the last step and reaches the ordinary foreleg gift that our פרק is about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The chain goes: right thigh, then the foreleg of sacrifices, then the foreleg of חולין. Each step is linked by a word in the פסוק, so the 'right side' rule passes all the way to the חולין gift.

keyTerms.meaning: Ordinary, non-holy animals
You shall give

steps.whatToRemember: There are two sources that the foreleg gift must be the right one: 'הזרוע' (the most important foreleg), or this chain from 'שוק הימין' through 'תרומה' and 'תתנו'.

phrases.english: How do I know about the foreleg of ordinary animals?
The פסוק says 'you shall give.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the chain that started in step 29.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The foreleg of an ordinary animal given to the כהן is the right one, learned through 'תתנו'.

steps.title: The jaw's limit seems to clash with a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends the jaw at the top ring of the windpipe, but a ברייתא says the slaughter area is taken along with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: What counts as the jaw? From the jaw joint down to the top ring of the windpipe. But a ברייתא teaches that he takes the jaw and the slaughter area together with it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's definition of the jaw. It then challenges it with a ברייתא that seems to give the כהן more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proper place for שחיטה is lower than the top ring of the windpipe. So if the כהן gets the slaughter area too, the jaw reaches past the limit the משנה set. The two sources seem to disagree about how much meat the כהן gets.

keyTerms.meaning: The jaw, one of the three gifts given to the כהן
Joint
The top ring of the windpipe
The area on the throat where שחיטה is done

phrases.english: What is the jaw?
From the joint of the jaw
until the top ring of the windpipe.
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
He takes it, and the slaughter area with it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from where the gifts come from in the פסוקים to the exact size of the jaw
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's lower limit for the jaw: the top ring of the windpipe
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא includes the slaughter area, which lies past that limit

steps.title: The two sources follow different תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The משנה follows the רבנן, and the ברייתא follows רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not a problem. This one follows the רבנן, and that one follows רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that each source follows a different opinion. The next step shows where that opinion comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The amount the כהן gets is the same in both sources: down to the top ring. They only differ in what they call that upper zone. For רבי חנינא it is also a valid place for שחיטה, so the ברייתא calls it a 'slaughter area.'

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the two sources can both be right
The majority of the sages

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי חנינא gives the כהן more meat. Both sides stop at the top ring. The only question is whether that zone can be called a slaughter area.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
This one follows the Rabbis,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is our משנה, and 'that one' in the next line is the ברייתא.

phrases.english: and that one follows Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא רַבָּנַן, וְהָא רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 31
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different תנאים: each source follows a different view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא gives the כהן more than the משנה does
steps.terutzMaskana: The amount is the same. Only the label 'slaughter area' depends on רבי חנינא's view.

steps.title: The source for רבי חנינא's view: slipped שחיטה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס allows שחיטה where the knife slipped up into the upper zone.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: שחיטה where the knife slipped upward is invalid. רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס testified that such שחיטה is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that proves רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס holds this view, supporting the answer just given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the knife slipped above the normal place toward the head, the רבנן say the שחיטה is invalid. רבי חנינא says it is valid. So for him the upper zone, which is part of the jaw, really is a 'slaughter area,' and that is why the ברייתא uses that name.

keyTerms.meaning: שחיטה where the knife slipped above the proper place, toward the head
Invalid
Valid
Testified: passed on a teaching he had received

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:
Slipped slaughter is invalid,
phrases.notes: This is the view of the רבנן: the knife went up past the proper zone.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus testified
about slipped slaughter that it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 32 by showing רבי חנינא's view
steps.raayaObject: That רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס treats the upper zone as a valid place for שחיטה

steps.title: Another answer: 'with it' means with the animal
steps.stepSummary: Both sources follow the רבנן; 'with it' means the slaughter area stays with the animal, not with the כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you like, say that both follow the רבנן. What does 'with it' mean? With the animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer that does not need רבי חנינא at all. It reads the word 'עמה' differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, 'with it' was read as 'with the jaw,' so the slaughter area went to the כהן. Now it is read as 'with the animal': the jaw is taken away, but the slaughter area is left for the owner. So the ברייתא agrees with the משנה's limit.

keyTerms.meaning: If you wish, say: introduces another possible answer
With it; here, with the animal

steps.whatToRemember: The jaw goes from the jaw joint to the top ring of the windpipe. The ברייתא either calls that zone a 'slaughter area' because of רבי חנינא, or it means the slaughter area stays with the animal.

phrases.english: If you wish, say:
both this and that follow the Rabbis,
and what does 'with it' mean?
With the animal.
phrases.notes: So the slaughter area stays with the owner and is not given to the כהן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to step 31, apart from the one in steps 32-33
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the word differently: 'עמה' refers to the animal
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'With it' means with the jaw, so it goes to the כהן
steps.terutzMaskana: 'With it' means with the animal, so it stays with the owner, and both sources follow the רבנן

steps.title: Hadran: Closing the chapter of the foreleg and the jaw
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא formally closes the chapter called הזרוע והלחיים with the traditional הדרן line.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter of 'The Foreleg and the Jaw.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is not a new argument. It is the traditional closing line that marks the end of the פרק called הזרוע והלחיים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words הדרן עלך mean 'we will return to you.' Learners say them to show that they have finished this chapter and hope to come back and learn it again. The name of the chapter comes from its opening words in the משנה: הזרוע והלחיים, the foreleg and the jaw.

keyTerms.meaning: 'We will return to you': the traditional line said at the end of a chapter of גמרא
The foreleg: one of the gifts from a slaughtered animal that is given to the כהן
The jaw (the cheeks): another of the gifts given to the כהן

steps.whatToRemember: This chapter was about the gifts the כהן gets from a slaughtered animal: the foreleg, the jaw, and the stomach. It ended by working out exactly where the jaw ends, from the jaw joint to the top ring of the windpipe. The גמרא gave two answers for the ברייתא's 'slaughter area': it follows רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס, or 'with it' means the slaughter area stays with the animal.

phrases.english: We will return to you,
phrases.notes: This is the traditional goodbye at the end of every chapter, a hope to come back and learn it again.

phrases.english: [chapter] 'The Foreleg and the Jaw.'

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: None: this is a standard chapter-closing formula
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 34 resolved the last contradiction about where the jaw ends, the chapter formally closes here.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פרק of הזרוע והלחיים, which dealt with the gifts of the foreleg, jaw, and stomach given to the כהן, is now complete.
